Grouter distills routing structure from a mature MoE into a preemptive router, decoupling routing search from weight learning; reports 4.28x better pre-training data utilization and up to 33.5% throughput acceleration, with official ICML listing and official implementation.

title: GSRQ: Gain-Shape Residual Quantization for Sub-1-bit KV Cache
topic: KV cache / long-context / sub-1-bit quantization / residual vector quantization
why: ICML 2026 direct KV-cache compression work. GSRQ replaces standard K-means inside residual vector quantization with gain-shape K-means to preserve directional fidelity at extremely low bit rates; on LLaMA-3-8B at 1 bit it raises LongBench average accuracy from 11.34 to 33.54 versus VQLLM, making sub-1-bit KV storage materially more viable.

title: HARD-KV: Head-Adaptive Regularization for Decoding-time KV Compression
topic: KV cache compression / head-adaptive sparsity / vLLM-compatible runtime
why: ICML 2026 KV compression system bridging dynamic head-adaptive Top-p selection with rigid CUDA-Graph/PagedAttention layouts via cascade cache and contiguous physical rewriting; reports up to 2x throughput on 10k+ token reasoning.

title: HASTE: Hardware-Aware Dynamic Sparse Training for Large Output Spaces
topic: sparsity / GPU kernels / hardware-aware sparse training / large output layers / memory-compute efficiency
why: ICML 2026 Regular paper. HASTE introduces group-shared fixed fan-in sparsity plus a dense-head/sparse-tail decomposition for million-label output layers, explicitly co-designed for GPU execution with custom CUDA kernels. Kernel microbenchmarks report up to 4.4x forward and 25x backward speedup over standard fixed-fan-in sparsity while retaining competitive precision.

title: HeraSys: Collaborative Serving of Multiple LLM Workflows via Fine-Grained End-to-End Optimization
topic: agentic LLM serving / multi-workflow scheduling / reuse / adaptive batching
why: ICML 2026; cross-workflow node merging/reuse plus load-aware joint scheduling and adaptive batching; reports up to 2.17x lower P99 latency and 1.85x higher throughput.

title: HERMES: Towards Efficient and Verifiable Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs
topic: efficient reasoning / agent systems / verifiable reasoning / test-time compute
why: ICML 2026 efficient-reasoning agent. HERMES interleaves informal reasoning with Lean-based single-step verification and memory, improving mathematical reasoning while sharply reducing wasted inference; the paper reports up to roughly 80% fewer total inference FLOPs in difficult settings, making it a direct test-time-compute efficiency contribution rather than only a verification paper.

title: HexGen-3: A Fully Disaggregated LLM Serving Framework with Fine-Grained Heterogeneous Resource Autoscaling
topic: LLM serving / disaggregation / heterogeneous resource autoscaling
why: ICML 2026; fully disaggregated inference with phase/operator-level heterogeneous resource autoscaling for cost-effective LLM serving.

title: HilbertA: Hilbert-Curve–Aligned Sparse Attention for 2D Structured Data
topic: efficient attention / diffusion acceleration / multimodal inference / GPU-aligned sparse attention / hardware-aware token layout
why: ICML 2026 main-conference poster confirmed by official ICML Downloads, OpenReview yhMt5V4FNb, and the first-author homepage. HilbertA maps 2D image tokens along a Hilbert curve so spatial locality becomes contiguous GPU memory access, with shifted windows and a shared region for cross-tile communication. Reported results include up to 4.16x attention and 1.44x end-to-end acceleration on Flux.1-dev and 2.30x attention / 1.57x TTFT speedup on Qwen3-VL-8B, making it a direct hardware-aware sparse-attention canonical.

title: HybridFlow: Resource-Adaptive Subtask Routing for Efficient Edge-Cloud LLM Inference
topic: edge-cloud LLM inference / adaptive routing / parallel subtask execution / latency-cost optimization
why: ICML 2026. Edge-cloud LLM inference framework decomposes each query into a dependency-aware DAG, executes newly unlocked subtasks in parallel, and routes each subtask online between edge and cloud using a learned benefit-cost utility under latency/token/API budgets; official ICML repository verified.

title: IAPO: Information-Aware Policy Optimization for Token-Efficient Reasoning
why: ICML 2026. Information-theoretic token-wise advantages suppress low-utility reasoning while preserving or improving correctness; reports up to 36% reasoning-length reduction across reasoning datasets.

title: Improving Visual Token Reduction via Rectifying Distortions for Efficient Multimodal LLM Inference
topic: multimodal / MLLM inference / visual token reduction / token merging
why: ICML 2026; RESTORE corrects positional and attention distortions introduced by visual-token reduction and improves multiple pruning/merging baselines while retaining the computational benefits; official author code is available.

title: Incremental BPE Tokenization
topic: LLM serving / tokenization runtime / streaming inference / incremental BPE
why: ICML 2026 Spotlight. Provides exact incremental BPE tokenization for every prefix with O(log^2 t) worst-case work per appended byte, supports eager streaming output, and reports up to ~3x speedup over Hugging Face tokenizers with significant latency reductions versus tiktoken on pathological inputs. This is a direct front-end/runtime optimization for streaming and agentic LLM serving rather than a tokenizer-quality paper.

title: IndexMem: Learned KV-Cache Eviction with Latent Memory for Long-Context LLM Inference
topic: KV cache eviction / latent memory / bounded-memory long-context inference
why: ICML 2026 learned KV-eviction framework with a latent-memory residual path for evicted tokens; improves long-context retrieval and RULER/LongBench under bounded cache budgets, with up to 25-point gains under aggressive eviction.

title: InfoFlow KV: Information-Flow-Aware KV Recomputation for Long Context
topic: KV cache / long-context RAG / selective recomputation
why: ICML 2026 direct long-context inference paper that treats selective KV recomputation as information flow and improves RAG/VLM long-context quality under comparable efficiency budgets.

title: INT vs. FP: A Comprehensive Study of Fine-Grained Low-bit Quantization Formats
topic: quantization / fine-grained low-bit formats / MXINT / MXFP / NVINT / NVFP / hardware-algorithm co-design
why: ICML 2026. Systematically compares fine-grained INT and FP quantization formats across granularities, showing an accuracy/efficiency crossover and that MXINT8 can outperform MXFP8 while offering better area/energy efficiency; also introduces symmetric clipping for nearly lossless MXINT8 low-bit training.

title: IO-Adam: Rethinking Memory-Efficient Adaptive Optimizers from Gradient Computation
topic: distributed training / memory-efficient optimizer / gradient decomposition
why: ICML 2026 main-conference memory-efficient optimizer. IO-Adam decomposes Adam second-moment statistics into input/output factors, reducing the second-moment memory from O(d_out*d_in) to O(d_out+d_in), and includes a LoMo-style fused backward/optimizer variant for further memory savings.

title: KernelBand: Steering LLM-based Kernel Optimization via Hardware-Aware Multi-Armed Bandits
topic: GPU kernel / LLM code generation / hardware-aware optimization / agentic compiler systems
why: ICML 2026 GPU-kernel optimization system. KernelBand formulates LLM-driven kernel optimization as hardware-aware multi-armed-bandit search, using profiling-based pruning and trace-driven clustering to balance exploration/exploitation; the official project reports up to 1.91x geometric-mean speedup with 39-140% higher Fast@1 over prior baselines.

title: KernelCraft: Benchmarking for Agentic Close-to-Metal Kernel Generation on Emerging Hardware
topic: GPU/NPU kernel / compiler / agentic code generation / emerging accelerators
why: ICML 2026 benchmark and systems framework for agentic low-level kernel generation on emerging accelerators. It evaluates function-calling agents across multiple custom ISAs and real/simulated hardware, with compile/simulation/correctness feedback loops, showing top agents can generate valid kernels for unseen ISAs and match or beat template/compiler baselines.

title: KernelFoundry: Hardware-aware evolutionary GPU kernel optimization
topic: GPU kernel / compiler / evolutionary optimization / hardware-aware agent systems
why: ICML 2026 distributed hardware-aware GPU-kernel optimization framework. KernelFoundry combines MAP-Elites quality-diversity search, meta-prompt evolution, template parameter optimization, profiler feedback, and a distributed multi-hardware test harness; the paper reports an average 2.3x speedup on KernelBench for SYCL and supports CUDA/SYCL kernel optimization.

title: Knapsack RL: Compute-Efficient Reinforcement Learning via Heterogeneous Rollout Allocation
topic: LLM RL / rollout allocation / training compute efficiency
why: ICML 2026; allocates heterogeneous rollout budgets under a fixed compute budget, improving effective-gradient ratio up to 40% and requiring roughly 2x less rollout compute for comparable performance than homogeneous allocation.

title: KnapSpec: Self-Speculative Decoding via Adaptive Layer Selection as a Knapsack Problem
topic: speculative decoding / adaptive layer selection / long-context inference
why: ICML 2026 training-free self-speculative decoding paper that models hardware/context-dependent attention and MLP costs and selects draft layers via parallel knapsack optimization; reports up to 1.47x wall-clock speedup while preserving exact target-model outputs.

title: Knowing When to Quit: A Principled Framework for Dynamic Abstention in LLM Reasoning
topic: efficient reasoning / dynamic abstention / early termination / test-time compute
why: ICML 2026; principled dynamic mid-generation abstention terminates unpromising reasoning traces, explicitly trading compute for information and reducing wasted chain-of-thought generation.

title: Latent Reasoning VLA: Latent Thinking and Prediction for Vision-Language-Action Models
topic: VLA / Physical AI serving / latent reasoning / efficient action inference
why: ICML 2026 protected Physical-AI efficiency paper. LaRA-VLA internalizes multimodal chain-of-thought into continuous latent reasoning, eliminating explicit reasoning-token generation and reporting up to 90% inference-latency reduction while improving VLA task performance; official training/evaluation code and weights are released.

title: LATMiX: Learnable Affine Transformations for Microscaling Quantization of LLMs
topic: quantization / microscaling MX / learnable affine transforms / low-bit LLM inference
why: ICML 2026 official Downloads lists LATMiX. It generalizes outlier-reducing rotations to learnable invertible affine transforms optimized for microscaling (MX) quantization and consistently improves low-bit LLM accuracy over strong baselines, directly filling modern hardware-oriented MX quantization coverage.

title: LazyAttention: Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Deferred Positional Encoding
topic: LLM serving / RAG / KV cache reuse / deferred positional encoding / attention kernels
why: ICML 2026 direct LLM-serving/KV-reuse systems work. LazyAttention defers positional encoding into attention kernels, enabling zero-copy position-agnostic KV reuse for RAG/ICL. It reports 1.37x lower TTFT and 1.40x higher inference throughput than Block-Attention under skewed document distributions while preserving output quality.

title: LC-QAT: Data-Efficient 2-Bit QAT for LLMs via Linear-Constrained Vector Quantization
topic: LLM quantization / 2-bit QAT / vector quantization / efficient deployment
why: ICML 2026 direct extreme-low-bit LLM deployment work. LC-QAT makes 2-bit vector-quantization QAT end-to-end differentiable via a linear-constrained codebook and achieves strong quality with only 0.1%-10% of conventional QAT training data, making 2-bit deployment substantially more practical.

title: LEAP: Zone-Aware MCTS for LLM Self-Speculative Decoding
topic: speculative decoding / self-speculative decoding / MCTS layer selection
why: ICML 2026 Poster; plug-and-play lossless self-speculative decoding using prefilling-derived redundancy and zone-aware MCTS to construct a per-instance lightweight draft model; reports 1.7x-2.0x inference speedup.

title: LearniBridge: Learnable Calibration of Feature Caching for Diffusion Models Acceleration
topic: video/image generation acceleration / diffusion transformer feature caching / low-rank cache calibration / inference acceleration
why: ICML 2026. LearniBridge learns prompt-invariant low-rank calibration updates for cached Diffusion Transformer features using lightweight LoRA and only 3-5 training samples; reported acceleration reaches 5.87x on FLUX, 5.75x on HunyuanVideo, and 4.10x on Wan2.1 with improved VBench at the latter operating point.

title: Learning Query-Aware Budget-Tier Routing for Runtime Agent Memory
topic: efficient reasoning / agent systems / runtime memory / adaptive compute routing / performance-cost control
why: ICML 2026. BudgetMem performs runtime, query-aware memory construction with Low/Mid/High budget tiers and a lightweight RL router, explicitly optimizing performance-cost trade-offs across implementation, reasoning and model-capacity tiers on LoCoMo, LongMemEval and HotpotQA.

title: Learning to Evict from Key-Value Cache
topic: KV cache / long-context inference / learned eviction / reinforcement learning
why: ICML 2026 Apple work introducing KV Policy (KVP), lightweight per-head RL agents that learn future-utility-based eviction rankings from generation traces; outperforms heuristic eviction across RULER up to 128K and multi-turn dialogue while requiring no modification to the base LLM or extra inference passes.

title: Learning to Share: Selective Memory for Efficient Parallel Agentic Systems
topic: efficient agent systems / parallel agents / shared memory / computation reuse
why: ICML 2026. Introduces learned shared memory for parallel agent teams so useful intermediate steps can be reused across trajectories while controlling context growth, reducing redundant computation and runtime while matching or improving task quality on AssistantBench and GAIA; official UCF implementation verified.

title: Least-Loaded Expert Parallelism: Load Balancing An Imbalanced Mixture-of-Experts
topic: MoE systems / expert parallelism / distributed inference / load balancing
why: ICML 2026 system/algorithmic infrastructure work for imbalanced MoE expert parallelism. LLEP dynamically reroutes excess tokens together with expert parameters to underutilized devices; authors report up to 5x speedup and 4x lower peak memory versus standard EP, including about 1.9x faster full-model inference for gpt-oss-120b.

title: Less Is More: Training-Free Sparse Attention with Global Locality for Efficient Reasoning
topic: efficient reasoning / sparse attention / KV-cache decoding
why: ICML 2026; training-free cross-head unified sparse attention for long reasoning. Official author/Princeton pages confirm acceptance; reports lossless AIME-24 accuracy with up to 87.5% fewer attended tokens and about 1.13x end-to-end generation speedup.

title: Less Token, More Signal: MoE Expert Pruning via Critical Token Selection
topic: MoE systems / expert pruning / memory-efficient inference
why: ICML 2026 Poster. STEP uses critical-token-guided expert importance with loss-aware evaluation and lightweight knowledge preservation; on Qwen3-30B with 50% expert sparsity it nearly halves memory, improves throughput by about 1.5x, and completes pruning in under 10 minutes.

title: LFQ: Logit-aware Final-block Quantization for Boosting the Generation Quality of Low-Bit Quantized LLMs
topic: LLM quantization / PTQ / long-form generation quality
why: ICML 2026 direct low-bit LLM PTQ paper addressing long-generation quality degradation through logit-aware final-block quantization; complements block-wise PTQ and reasoning-focused deployment routes.

title: LiftQuant: Continuous Bit-Width Control for Pareto-Optimal LLM Deployment
topic: quantization / fractional bit-width / memory-constrained LLM deployment
why: ICML 2026 Spotlight. Continuous effective bit-width enables Pareto-optimal LLM fitting under exact GPU memory budgets; a 70B model can be fit at ~2.4 bits with a hardware-friendly decoding path.

title: Light Forcing: Accelerating Autoregressive Video Diffusion via Sparse Attention
topic: video generation acceleration / autoregressive video / sparse attention / kernels
why: ICML 2026 direct video-generation efficiency work; chunk-aware hierarchical sparse attention gives ~1.2-1.3x E2E alone and ~2-3x with deployment optimizations; official repository provides sparse kernels and quantized deployment paths.

title: LightningRL: Breaking the Accuracy-Parallelism Trade-off of Block-wise dLLMs via Reinforcement Learning
topic: diffusion LLM / parallel decoding / RL post-training / inference acceleration
why: ICML 2026 direct dLLM acceleration; RL optimizes speed-quality Pareto frontier and the official implementation reports 336 TPS on H100, ~3.2x faster than SDAR while maintaining high accuracy.

title: LiME: Lightweight Mixture of Experts for Efficient Multimodal Multi-task Learning
topic: multimodal efficiency / lightweight MoE / parameter-efficient fine-tuning / adaptive routing
why: ICML 2026 multimodal-efficiency work. LiME replaces per-expert adapter replication with shared PEFT plus lightweight expert modulation and zero-parameter routing, using up to 4x fewer trainable parameters and up to 29% faster training than MoE-PEFT baselines.

title: LiMuon: Light and Fast Muon Optimizer for Large Models
topic: LLM training efficiency / memory-efficient optimizer / Muon
why: ICML 2026; lowers Muon optimizer memory with randomized SVD and improves stochastic sample complexity via variance reduction, with experiments on Mamba-130M, Qwen2.5-0.5B and ViT showing practical training-efficiency gains.

title: LK Losses: Direct Acceptance Rate Optimization for Speculative Decoding
topic: speculative decoding / draft-model training / acceptance optimization
why: ICML 2026. Replaces KL-proxy draft training with acceptance-aligned LK objectives; across four draft architectures and six target models (8B-685B), improves average acceptance length by up to about 8-10% with no inference overhead and integrates directly into existing speculator training pipelines.

title: Locally Coherent Parallel Decoding in Diffusion Language Models
topic: diffusion language model / parallel decoding / local autoregressive decoding / efficient code generation / inference acceleration
why: ICML 2026 main-track paper from IBM Research/ETH Zurich. CoDiLA combines global diffusion-LM parallel generation with a compact local autoregressive decoder operating on diffusion latents, preserving sub-linear generation latency while repairing local syntactic dependencies that otherwise break parallel decoding. It establishes an improved accuracy-speed Pareto frontier for code generation and is a direct diffusion-LM parallel-decoding efficiency work.

title: LoKiFormer: Locality-aware Attention with Decoupled Knowledge Memory for Efficient Large Language Model Pretraining
topic: LLM pretraining efficiency / efficient attention / explicit knowledge memory
why: ICML 2026; introduces Local Fusion Attention plus a decoupled parametric Knowledge Memory Module to reduce redundant local modeling and separate knowledge storage from computation; reports 1.33x faster pretraining convergence than Transformer baselines.

title: Long-Context Modeling with Dynamic Hierarchical Sparse Attention for Memory-Constrained LLM Inference
topic: efficient attention / long-context LLM inference / on-device inference
why: ICML 2026 Spotlight; DHSA predicts content-dependent sparse attention online with variable-length hierarchical routing and memory-efficient GPU/CPU backends; reports up to 10x prefill speedup at 128K and enables 100K context on a single 24GB GPU while preserving near-dense accuracy.

title: LoSA: Locality Aware Sparse Attention for Block-Wise Diffusion Language Models
topic: efficient attention / diffusion language model acceleration / KV reuse / sparse attention / long-context inference
why: ICML 2026. Addresses KV Inflation in block-wise diffusion language models by reusing cached prefix-attention for stable tokens and applying sparse attention only to active tokens. It reports 1.54x lower attention density and up to 4.14x attention speedup on RTX A6000 while preserving near-dense accuracy.

title: LRAgent: Efficient KV Cache Sharing for Multi-LoRA LLM Agents
topic: KV cache sharing / multi-LoRA agent serving / Flash-LoRA-Attention
why: Multi-LoRA agent serving framework that decomposes KV cache into a shared base component plus low-rank adapter-dependent cache; reports up to 2.46x throughput, 4.44x TTFT reduction and about 3x KV-cache memory reduction while preserving accuracy.

title: LSGQuant: Layer-Sensitivity Guided Quantization for One-Step Diffusion Real-World Video Super-Resolution
topic: quantization / video generation acceleration / diffusion transformer / low-bit inference
why: ICML 2026 direct diffusion/video quantization work. Layer-sensitivity guided PTQ combines dynamic-range-aware activation quantization, variance-oriented layer training, and quantization-aware optimization to compress one-step DiT video super-resolution while preserving near-full-precision quality; author publication page and ICML listing confirm venue, and official author repository is verified.

title: LUGS: Latent-aware Guidance for Efficient Unmasking in Diffusion Large Language Models
topic: diffusion language model acceleration / efficient decoding / unmasking policy / latent guidance
why: ICML 2026 poster. Direct dLLM inference-efficiency work: uses latent hidden-state guidance to improve unmasking decisions beyond local confidence/entropy heuristics, targeting better quality-efficiency trade-offs in parallel diffusion decoding.

title: M+Adam: Low-Precision Training via Additive-Multiplicative Optimization
topic: low-precision training / FP8 FP4 / optimizer / memory efficiency
why: ICML 2026. Combines additive and multiplicative updates to train directly with BF16, FP8, and FP4 master weights without higher-precision copies; improves low-precision LLaMA-style pretraining across model scales and budgets.

title: ManifoldKV: Training-Free KV Cache Compression via Euclidean Outlier Detection
topic: KV cache compression / training-free eviction / long-context inference
why: ICML 2026 training-free KV compression using Euclidean outlier detection; improves multi-key retrieval robustness and restores 64K-context performance with windowed scoring while requiring minimal implementation changes.

title: MAPS: Memory-Aware Predictive Scheduling Framework for Large Language Model Serving
topic: LLM serving / disaggregated inference / predictive scheduling / memory-aware scheduling
why: ICML 2026 Poster; device-assisted speculative output-length prediction overlapped with cloud prefilling plus uncertainty-calibrated hierarchical scheduling for memory-bound disaggregated decode; reports 42.6% lower mean end-to-end latency and up to 84.8% lower tail latency versus three serving baselines.

title: MedCoG: Maximizing LLM Inference Density in Medical Reasoning via Meta-Cognitive Regulation
topic: efficient reasoning / agent systems / inference-time compute allocation / adaptive knowledge use
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper. Meta-cognitive regulation avoids indiscriminate inference scaling by adaptively deciding when and how to use procedural, episodic, and factual knowledge; reports roughly 5.5x inference density on difficult medical reasoning benchmarks.

title: MemOCR: Layout-Aware Visual Memory for Efficient Long-Horizon Reasoning
topic: efficient reasoning / agent memory / multimodal memory compression / long-horizon context efficiency
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper confirmed by official/author sources and Meituan repository. MemOCR compresses growing interaction histories into adaptive visual layouts and reports about 8x token-efficiency gain under extreme budgets, making it a canonical context/memory-efficiency route for long-horizon agents.

title: Memory-Efficient LLM Pretraining via Minimalist Optimizer Design
topic: distributed training / memory-efficient LLM pretraining / optimizer-state reduction
why: ICML 2026 memory-efficient LLM pretraining work. SCALE combines column-wise gradient normalization with first-order momentum only on the output layer, matching or exceeding Adam while using only about 35-45% of total memory across 60M-1B models and outperforming memory-efficient baselines such as GaLore/Fira/APOLLO; the official OptimAI-Lab repository provides the implementation.

title: Memory-Efficient LLM Training with Dynamic Sparsity: From Stability to Practical Scaling
topic: LLM training efficiency / dynamic sparsity / memory-efficient optimization
why: ICML 2026; Sparse Memory-Efficient Training stabilizes dynamic sparse LLM pretraining with optimizer warm-up and density-aware learning-rate scaling while storing gradients and optimizer states only for active parameters, making sparse pretraining materially memory-efficient.

title: Mining Tensor/Neuron-Level Sparsity to Maximize Mixture-of-Experts Potential in Post-Training and Inference
topic: MoE systems / post-training sparsity / token-expert dropping / expert partition / inference acceleration
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper, with the same author set as the earlier arXiv title DualSparse-MoE. It exploits tensor-level and neuron-level sparsity after pretraining via expert partitioning, threshold-based token-expert dropping, partial partition/reconstruction, and load-imbalance-aware execution. Reported inference-only results reach up to 1.41x MoE speedup with under 0.5% accuracy loss, making it a direct MoE deployment-efficiency canonical.

title: MixFP4: Enhancing NVFP4 with Adaptive FP4/INT4 Block Representations
topic: quantization / FP4-INT4 micro-format / Tensor Core co-design / LLM inference
why: ICML 2026 poster. MixFP4 extends NVFP4 with per-block E2M1/E1M2 selection while reusing the FP8 block-scale sign bit for zero-extra-metadata format tagging and a unified internal compute representation; reports improved 4-bit robustness with only 3.1% area and 1.5% power overhead in the proposed Tensor Core support.

title: MixQuant: Pushing the Limits of Block Rotations in Post-Training Quantization
topic: quantization / post-training quantization / block Hadamard rotation / low-bit LLM inference
why: ICML 2026 direct low-bit PTQ work. MixQuant/PeRQ analyzes the limits of block Hadamard rotations and calibrates permutation-based activation-mass redistribution before rotation, then folds permutations into model weights so deployment adds no inference overhead; experiments recover up to about 90% of full-vector-rotation perplexity for INT4 Llama3-1B at block size 16.

title: Mixture of Distributions Matters: Dynamic Sparse Attention for Efficient Video Diffusion Transformers
topic: video generation acceleration / diffusion / dynamic sparse attention
why: ICML 2026 video-DiT efficiency work. MOD-DiT models evolving attention sparsity with a mixture-of-distributions approximation plus online block masking, avoiding repeated expensive sparsity sampling while preserving generation quality and accelerating video diffusion attention.

title: Model-Preserving Adaptive Rounding
topic: quantization / LLM PTQ / adaptive rounding / model-preserving compression
why: ICML 2026 Cornell RelaxML quantization paper introducing YAQA, an adaptive-rounding PTQ method using full-model/Kronecker-factored Hessian approximations rather than layer-local activation error. Primary arXiv reports about 30% lower KL divergence to the original model across models/quantizers with no inference overhead; official Christopher De Sa publication page lists it as ICML 2026.

title: MoSE: Mixture of Slimmable Experts for Efficient and Adaptive Language Models
topic: MoE / conditional computation / slimmable experts / adaptive inference FLOPs
why: ICML 2026 efficient-MoE work. MoSE makes each expert slimmable, allowing runtime control over both which experts execute and how much of each expert executes. It shifts the accuracy-compute Pareto frontier toward lower inference FLOPs and supports budget-aware runtime width selection.

title: MoshiRAG: Asynchronous Knowledge Retrieval for Full-Duplex Speech Language Models
topic: multimodal serving / full-duplex speech LM / asynchronous RAG / real-time inference
why: ICML 2026 real-time multimodal serving work. MoshiRAG keeps a compact full-duplex speech-language interface while asynchronously retrieving stronger knowledge sources during the natural response gap, improving factuality without sacrificing real-time interactivity; the official implementation includes production-oriented Rust inference code.

title: Motion-Aware Caching for Efficient Autoregressive Video Generation
topic: autoregressive video generation / cache reuse / diffusion acceleration
why: ICML 2026. MotionCache uses token-level motion-aware cache reuse instead of coarse chunk skipping; reports 6.28x on SkyReels-V2 and 1.64x on MAGI-1 with very small quality loss.

title: Multi-Head LatentMoE and Head Parallel: Communication-Efficient and Deterministic MoE Parallelism
topic: MoE systems / distributed training / communication-efficient parallelism / deterministic routing / IO-aware execution
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper. Multi-Head LatentMoE with Head Parallel achieves O(1) communication cost with respect to activated experts, fully balanced deterministic traffic, and IO-aware routing/expert computation; compared with MoE expert parallelism it reports up to 1.61x faster training at identical performance.

title: Multipole Semantic Attention: A Fast Approximation of Softmax Attention for Pretraining
topic: efficient attention / long-context pretraining / attention approximation
why: ICML 2026. Semantic clustering plus multipole expansions gives subquadratic/drop-in attention; reports 3x isolated-layer speedup over cuDNN FlashAttention at 8k and material end-to-end long-context pretraining runtime reductions with small loss degradation.

title: MVR-cache: Optimizing Semantic Caching via Multi-Vector Retrieval and Learned Prompt Segmentation
topic: LLM serving / semantic cache / response reuse / retrieval / inference cost reduction
why: ICML 2026 semantic-caching system for LLM serving. MVR-cache learns prompt segmentation and uses multi-vector retrieval/MaxSim to improve semantically safe response-cache reuse; experiments report up to 37% higher cache hit rate at the same correctness guarantee, directly reducing repeated LLM inference cost and latency.

title: NanoFLUX: Distillation-Driven Compression of Large Text-to-Image Generation Models for Mobile Devices
topic: image generation acceleration / flow matching / model compression / mobile edge AI / distillation
why: ICML 2026 official Downloads lists NanoFLUX as a main-conference paper. NanoFLUX progressively compresses FLUX.1-Schnell from a 17B teacher to a 2.4B mobile text-to-image model using DiT pruning, token downsampling, and text-encoder distillation, reporting 512x512 generation in about 2.5 seconds on a mobile device.

title: NanoQuant: Efficient Sub-1-Bit Quantization of Large Language Models
topic: quantization / sub-1-bit PTQ / custom kernels / consumer-GPU deployment
why: ICML 2026. Sub-1-bit post-training quantization with custom low-bit kernels; reports extreme model-memory compression and practical consumer-GPU deployment while preserving useful accuracy.

title: NanoSpec: Accelerating Speculative Decoding using Minimalist In-Context Vocabularies
topic: speculative decoding / active-vocabulary pruning / GPU runtime
why: ICML 2026. Training-free speculative-decoding co-design that restricts draft computation to a small dynamic in-context vocabulary and combines asynchronous gathering/GPU-resident state to reduce draft cost and improve end-to-end speed.

title: Native Parallel Reasoner: Reasoning in Parallelism via Self-Distilled Reinforcement Learning
topic: efficient reasoning / parallel reasoning / SGLang runtime / reinforcement learning / inference acceleration
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper. NPR trains models to reason with genuine parallel execution rather than serial autoregressive traces; its NPR Engine refactors SGLang memory/flow control for parallel RL and inference, reporting up to 4.6x inference acceleration across reasoning benchmarks.

title: NeUQI: Near-Optimal Uniform Quantization Parameter Initialization for Low-Bit LLMs
topic: LLM quantization / low-bit PTQ / uniform quantization / parameter initialization / consumer-GPU deployment
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper confirmed by the senior-author publication list. NeUQI replaces suboptimal Min-Max initialization with efficient near-optimal initialization for uniform low-bit PTQ and is designed to improve practical memory/decoding efficiency on consumer-grade hardware.

title: No Retraining at Edge: Efficient Resource-Aware Mixed-Precision Quantization via Federated Supernet Learning
topic: edge AI / mixed-precision quantization / federated supernet / resource-adaptive deployment
why: ICML 2026 Poster. DFMPQ trains a weight-sharing mixed-precision federated supernet once, then derives resource-aware quantized subnets for changing edge constraints without retraining; directly targets heterogeneous edge deployment cost.

title: NorMuon: Making Muon more efficient and scalable
topic: distributed LLM training / optimizer / FSDP2 / training efficiency
why: ICML 2026 Spotlight. Neuron-wise normalized Muon with a distributed FSDP2 implementation; Microsoft reports 21.74% better training efficiency than Adam and 11.31% improvement over Muon on 1.1B pretraining with comparable memory footprint.

title: Not All Prefills Are Equal: PPD Disaggregation for Multi-turn LLM Serving
topic: LLM serving / prefill-decode disaggregation / multi-turn KV reuse
why: ICML 2026; dynamic PPD routing reuses cached KV for Turn 2+ append-prefill on decode nodes and reports about 68% lower Turn 2+ TTFT while controlling TPOT and KV-transfer congestion.

title: OBCache: Optimal Brain KV Cache Pruning for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
topic: KV cache / long-context inference / output-aware eviction / pruning

Q-Sched is a scheduler-level post-training quantization method for few-step diffusion models: it keeps quantized weights fixed and learns quantization-aware preconditioning coefficients with a reference-free calibration loss, yielding a 4x model-size reduction while matching or improving full-precision image quality on fast diffusion backbones.

QiMeng-PerceptOS is a perception-driven closed-loop framework for application-specific OS-kernel optimization: it converts runtime telemetry into semantic fingerprints, uses a bi-level hierarchical induction tree for global search/pruning, and applies posterior enhancement to suppress hallucinated tuning trajectories. Across diverse workloads it reaches 296.6% of default Redis throughput and exceeds strong baselines by 32.6% within 15 iterations, making it a direct AI-infra / OS-kernel optimization canonical rather than a generic LLM-agent paper.

title: QTALE: Quantization-Robust Token-Adaptive Layer Execution for LLMs
topic: quantization / token-adaptive layer execution / dynamic depth / efficient LLM deployment
why: ICML 2026 main-conference paper. QTALE jointly enables token-adaptive layer skipping for FLOPs reduction and weight quantization for memory reduction, using diverse-path fine-tuning plus inference-time execution-ratio adjustment; reported quantized adaptive models stay within 0.5% of quantization-only accuracy on CommonsenseQA-style evaluations while retaining the deployment savings of both techniques.

topic: LLM quantization / 2-bit QAT / residual binarization / matmul-free inference / GPU acceleration

why: ICML 2026 regular/poster direct MoE deployment-efficiency work. RaGEP performs rank-aware inter-layer expert-budget allocation and spectral-salience intra-layer pruning to reduce static expert footprint and inference cost on memory-constrained hardware while preserving task quality; ICML Downloads and author/CAS official pages confirm acceptance.

With dilation D, attention FLOPs and KV-cache size fall by D; experiments report near-dense accuracy at D=16 and about one-point average loss at D=64 for larger models, giving a direct flexible inference-time compute/memory knob without training a separate sparse model.

why: ICML 2026 official Downloads inventory paper. Predicts future reward as a function of additional thinking tokens to stop unpromising chains and allocate test-time compute adaptively, directly reducing reasoning cost.

why: Direct diffusion inference acceleration. Chebyshev-inspired stable extrapolation skips expensive DiT block executions; reports up to 3.68x latency speedup and 5.12x FLOPs reduction across DiT-XL/2, PixArt-Sigma and FLUX.1-dev.

title: Chipmunk: Training-Free Acceleration of Diffusion Transformers with Dynamic Column-Sparse Deltas
why: Chipmunk dynamic column-sparse DiT kernels and activation reuse deliver up to 2.16x HunyuanVideo and 1.41x FLUX speedup, or 3.72x with step caching; GPU sparse-gather kernel co-design.

title: CODA: Rewriting Transformer Blocks as GEMM-Epilogue Programs
why: CODA rewrites Transformer non-attention operators into GEMM epilogues to avoid memory-bound intermediate tensor traffic and enable on-chip fusion.

title: DeepSeek-V2: A Strong, Economical, and Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Language Model
why: DeepSeek-V2 MLA+MoE architecture achieves 93.3% KV cache reduction and up to 5.76x generation throughput; foundational efficiency architecture.

title: EdgeFlow: Fast Cold Starts for LLMs on Mobile Devices
topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / mobile LLM inference / quantization / NPU runtime
why: EdgeFlow is a direct mobile-LLM inference system targeting cold-start TTFT. It combines NPU-aware adaptive weight precision, SIMD-friendly packing, and a fine-grained CPU-NPU pipeline; the paper reports up to 4.07x lower cold-start latency than llama.cpp/MNN/llm.npu at comparable accuracy. First-party author publication page independently lists the paper and primary PDF.

title: Escaping the Cognitive Well: Efficient Competition Math with Off-the-Shelf Models
why: Cognitive Well mitigation with conjecture extraction and independent verification achieves strong IMO proof results at about $31 per question, orders of magnitude cheaper than prior large-scale inference pipelines.

title: Exploring Diffusion Transformer Designs via Grafting
why: Diffusion Transformer grafting replaces attention/MLP operators and restructures depth with <2% pretraining compute; reports 1.43x text-to-image inference speedup with <2% GenEval drop.

title: Fantastic Pretraining Optimizers and Where to Find Them II: Hyperball Optimization
why: Hyperball optimizer wrapper reports 20-30% token-equivalent pretraining speedup over weight-decay baselines for Qwen3-style models up to 1.2B.

title: FlashVLA: Streaming Action Decoding for Fast and Asynchronous VLA Inference
topic: Physical AI / VLA serving / streaming action decoding
why: Protected Physical-AI direct serving work. FlashVLA jointly targets low-latency inference and temporally consistent asynchronous execution and reports >=30 Hz control frequency on one GPU in real-world deployment.

title: FP6-LLM: Efficiently Serving Large Language Models Through FP6-Centric Algorithm-System Co-Design
why: FP6-LLM TC-FPx Tensor Core kernel co-design addresses irregular FP6 weights and dequantization, reporting 1.69-2.65x throughput versus FP16.

title: Frame Context Packing and Drift Prevention in Next-Frame-Prediction Video Diffusion Models
topic: Video / Image Generation Acceleration; Diffusion / Flow Acceleration
why: FramePack compresses video-frame contexts into a fixed budget and supports long video generation with larger training batches; official first-party paper and public implementation verified.

title: Goedel-Architect: Streamlining Formal Theorem Proving with Blueprint Generation and Refinement
why: Goedel-Architect parallel blueprint-driven theorem-proving agent reports up to 500x lower cost than comparable open-source pipelines with high benchmark accuracy.

title: Griffin: Mixing Gated Linear Recurrences with Local Attention for Efficient Language Models
why: Griffin hybrid gated linear recurrences and local attention matches Transformer training hardware efficiency while achieving lower inference latency and higher throughput at up to 14B parameters.

title: Hexa-MoE: Efficient and Heterogeneous-aware Training for Mixture-of-Experts
why: Heterogeneous MoE training system with specialized operators and pipeline-shared caching; official abstract reports 10–48% memory reduction and 0.5–4.3x speedup.

title: HybridStitch: Pixel and Timestep Level Model Stitching for Diffusion Acceleration
why: HybridStitch performs pixel/timestep-aware small-large model stitching to reduce diffusion inference cost.

title: HyMCache: A KV Cache Framework for Multi-Turn LLM Serving with CXL-Hybrid Memory
topic: LLM serving / KV cache / CXL-hybrid memory / disaggregated inference
why: Real CXL-HM prototype for TB-scale reusable KV in multi-turn/agentic serving. Request-level prefix prefetch and write buffering stage SSD-backed KV into device DRAM; reports 3.0x over local LMCache and 1.45x in PD-disaggregated serving at equal DRAM budget.

title: Identifying Sensitive Weights via Post-quantization Integral
why: PQI/ReQuant improves quantization sensitivity estimation and outlier handling, important for LLM low-bit PTQ.

title: InfLLM: Training-Free Long-Context Extrapolation for LLMs with an Efficient Context Memory
why: InfLLM enables training-free long-context extrapolation with external memory units and efficient token-relevant lookup, supporting up to 1,024K-token sequences with bounded active context.

title: Jetfire: Efficient and Accurate Transformer Pretraining with INT8 Data Flow and Per-Block Quantization
why: Jetfire INT8 transformer training uses INT8 data flow and per-block quantization, 1.42x training speedup and 1.49x memory reduction.

title: Joint Distillation for Fast Likelihood Evaluation and Sampling in Flow-based Models
why: F2D2 jointly distills flow sampling and likelihood evaluation, reducing neural function evaluations by roughly two orders of magnitude while preserving sample quality.

title: Just Noticeable Difference Modeling for Token Compression in Vision-Language-Action Models
topic: Physical AI / VLA token compression / KV reuse / pruning
why: Protected Physical-AI efficiency work. Action-JND explicitly optimizes safe VLA token compression for latency-sensitive closed-loop actions and applies to stale-KV reuse and token pruning on OpenVLA/OpenVLA-OFT.

title: Large Scale Diffusion Distillation via Score-Regularized Continuous-Time Consistency
why: Large-scale continuous-time consistency distillation tackles JVP/parallelism for fast image and video generation.

title: LEANN: A Low-Storage Vector Index
why: LEANN reduces vector index storage up to 50x with comparable RAG retrieval latency and accuracy; important retrieval infrastructure.

title: Multi-Segment Attention: Enabling Efficient KV-Cache Management for Faster Large Language Model Serving
topic: LLM serving / KV cache / efficient attention / agentic serving
why: AsymCache is a lossless computation-latency-aware KV-cache management system. It combines fused Multi-Segment Attention for non-contiguous KV regions, position/reuse-aware eviction, and adaptive chunking; reports up to 2.03x lower TTFT and 1.71x lower TPOT over recent baselines, plus up to 18.1% lower agent-job latency when integrated with Continuum.

title: NanoFlow: Towards Optimal Large Language Model Serving Throughput
why: NanoFlow overlaps GPU compute/memory/network via nano-batches; up to 1.91x serving throughput, foundational serving-systems work.

title: Nemotron 3 Super: Open, Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Hybrid Mamba-Transformer Model for Agentic Reasoning
topic: MoE inference, NVFP4, speculative decoding, agentic reasoning
why: Nemotron 3 Super combines NVFP4 pretraining, LatentMoE, and native multi-token-prediction speculative decoding; first-party abstract reports 2.2x/7.5x inference throughput over specified 120B baselines, with open checkpoints.

title: Occult: Optimizing Collaborative Communication across Experts for Accelerated Parallel MoE Training and Inference
why: ICML 2025; expert co-location and collaboration pruning reduce distributed MoE all-to-all communication; official abstract reports >1.5x speedup.

title: Organize then Retrieve: Hierarchical Memory Navigation for Efficient Agents
why: HORMA hierarchical agent memory cuts long-conversation token usage to at most 22.17% of baseline and reduces latency-critical retrieval.

title: Oscillation-Reduced MXFP4 Training for Vision Transformers
why: TetraJet MXFP4 transformer training addresses quantization oscillation; improves low-bit training accuracy with official code.

title: SageAttention2: Efficient Attention with Thorough Outlier Smoothing and Per-thread INT4 Quantization
why: SageAttention2 introduces INT4 Q/K, FP8 attention intermediates and outlier smoothing for fast accurate attention.

title: SageAttention: Accurate 8-Bit Attention for Plug-and-play Inference Acceleration
why: SageAttention delivers 8-bit attention acceleration for inference with precision preservation.

title: SAW-INT4: System-Aware 4-Bit KV-Cache Quantization for Real-World LLM Serving
why: SAW-INT4 integrates block-diagonal Hadamard rotation and token-wise INT4 quantization into fused paged KV-cache kernels with no measurable end-to-end overhead.

title: Search Your Block Floating Point Scales!
why: ScaleSearch optimizes BFP/NVFP4 scales and presents accelerated NVFP4 attention with reduced accuracy loss.

title: SHIELD: A Segmented Hierarchical Memory Architecture for Energy-Efficient LLM Inference on Edge NPUs
why: SHIELD proposes lifecycle-aware segmented eDRAM to reduce energy for edge-NPU LLM inference.

title: SLA2: Sparse-Linear Attention with Learnable Routing and QAT
why: SLA2 improves sparse-linear diffusion attention via learnable routing and quantization-aware training.

title: SLA: Beyond Sparsity in Diffusion Transformers via Fine-Tunable Sparse-Linear Attention
why: SLA sparse-linear DiT attention reports 13.7x attention-kernel and 2.2x end-to-end video generation speedups; official code available.

title: SpargeAttention2: Trainable Sparse Attention via Hybrid Top-k+Top-p Masking and Distillation Fine-Tuning
why: SpargeAttention2 achieves 95% sparse attention and 16.2x attention speedup for video diffusion, with official abstract reporting quality preservation.

title: SpargeAttention: Accurate and Training-free Sparse Attention Accelerating Any Model Inference
why: SpargeAttention training-free universal sparse attention accelerates language/image/video inference; official implementation.

title: Speculative Decoding for Autoregressive Video Generation
why: SDVG applies speculative decoding to autoregressive video diffusion with 1.59x speedup at 98.1% target quality; relevant to streaming video generation systems.

title: SPICE: Speculative Prefetching with Low-Rank Expert Surrogates and Heterogeneous Orchestration for MoE Inference Acceleration
topic: MoE systems / expert offload / heterogeneous inference
why: Direct MoE offloading systems work. Confidence-aware speculative expert prefetch plus CPU-GPU heterogeneous recovery targets PCIe expert-loading bottlenecks; reports up to 3.12x TPOT speedup.

title: STUN: Structured-Then-Unstructured Pruning for Scalable MoE Pruning
why: STUN scalable MoE expert+unstructured pruning with O(1) expert decision and 40% sparsity on 480B Arctic model in two H100 hours.

title: SwiftCache: Efficient LLM Serving for Multi-turn Conversations with Heterogeneous KV Cache Sharing
topic: LLM serving / KV cache / multi-turn agents / NVLink memory sharing
why: Collaborative serving system that lets heterogeneous colocated models donate idle GPU memory and NVLink bandwidth for cross-model KV-prefix sharing; reports up to 69% lower P99 TTFT and 3.98x longer supported context versus vLLM/SGLang.

title: Transformers to SSMs: Distilling Quadratic Knowledge to Subquadratic Models
why: MOHAWK distills Transformer mixing matrices into Mamba-2/SSM models with <1% of scratch pretraining data, enabling efficient subquadratic model transfer.

title: TreeGraft: Adaptive Multi-Drafter Grafting for Tree-Based Speculative Decoding
why: Fresh direct inference work from the official arXiv Friday 28 Aug new-submission inventory. Multi-drafter tree construction addresses the drafter latency-vs-quality trade-off and directly targets higher accepted length / lower target-model decoding cost.

title: TurboDiffusion: Accelerating Video Diffusion Models by 100-200 Times
why: TurboDiffusion integrates low-bit SageAttention, sparse-linear attention, step distillation and W8A8 for 100-200x reported video diffusion acceleration.

title: TurboServe: Serving Streaming Video Generation Efficiently and Economically
why: TurboServe explicitly optimizes multi-user multi-GPU streaming video generation serving, state retention and chunk-level scheduling.

title: Unleashing Scalable Context Parallelism for Foundation Models Pre-Training via FCP
why: FCP block-level context parallelism and sequence bin packing, near-linear scaling to 256 GPUs and 1.13–2.21x attention MFU; important distributed foundation-model training.

title: XGrammar: Flexible and Efficient Structured Generation Engine for Large Language Models
why: XGrammar constrained decoding/structured generation engine; up to 100x grammar speedup and near-zero overhead in LLM serving.

title: XQuant: Breaking the Memory Wall for LLM Inference with KV Cache Rematerialization
why: XQuant KV rematerialization reduces LLM inference memory up to 10x with near-FP16 accuracy; important KV/cache alternative.
